Cloud Cost Review - Q3 2024

Overview
This report covers cloud infrastructure spending for Northwind's production and staging environments across all regions from July 1 through September 30, 2024. Total spend was $2,340,000, up 18% from Q2 ($1,983,000) and 34% year-over-year.

Cost by Service
- Compute (instances, containers, functions): $1,120,000 (48% of total)
  - 67% of compute is reserved, 33% on-demand
  - Reserved instance utilization: 82% (target: 90%)
  - Function costs increased 45% due to new data pipeline jobs
- Storage: $540,000 (23% of total)
  - Object storage: $310,000, of which $89,000 is for analytics bucket barely accessed
  - Block storage: $180,000, 40% is older volume type that could be upgraded
  - File storage: $50,000, one team uses 78% of it
- Database: $410,000 (18% of total)
  - Relational: $290,000 across 14 instances, 6 under 15% CPU utilization
  - NoSQL: $78,000, on-demand mode costing 3x what provisioned would
  - Cache: $42,000, 2 clusters same size as prod but used for staging
- Networking: $180,000 (8% of total)
  - NAT Gateway: $67,000, us-east-1 NAT is $23,000 alone
  - CDN: $89,000, 30% of traffic to internal tools that don't need it
- Other: $90,000 (4% of total)

Savings Options
1. Right-size 6 underutilized database instances: $45,000/quarter
2. Convert NoSQL to provisioned with auto-scaling: $52,000/quarter
3. Upgrade block storage volumes: $27,000/quarter
4. Downsize staging cache clusters: $21,000/quarter
5. Add private endpoints to reduce NAT Gateway costs: $18,000/quarter
6. Archive cold analytics data: $36,000/quarter
7. Purchase reserved instances for on-demand compute: $67,000/quarter (requires 1-year commitment)
8. Remove CDN for internal tools: $27,000/quarter

Total potential savings: $293,000/quarter (12.5% of current spend)

Risks
- Right-sizing databases could impact performance if traffic spikes
- Reserved instance commitments lock us in for 1 year
- Archiving data requires analytics team sign-off, they may push back
- Converting NoSQL requires capacity planning, underestimating causes throttling
- Savings require engineering time (estimated 3-4 sprints)

Implementation Timeline
- Quick wins (items 2,3,4,8): 2-3 weeks, $127,000/quarter savings
- Medium effort (items 1,5,6): 4-6 weeks, $99,000/quarter savings
- Reserved instances (item 7): requires commitment decision, $67,000/quarter savings

Regional Breakdown
- us-east-1: $1,053,000 (45%)
- eu-west-1: $585,000 (25%)
- ap-southeast-1: $468,000 (20%)
- us-west-2: $234,000 (10%)

Open Questions
- Should we commit to 1-year reserved instances given uncertain growth? I don't know if we'll need more or less compute in 6 months
- Does anyone actually use analytics data older than 90 days? Analytics team hasn't responded

Reliability Review - Q3 2024

Overview
This report covers system reliability for Northwind's production platform from July 1 through September 30, 2024.

SLA Target: 99.95% uptime (21.9 minutes allowed downtime per month)
Actual: 99.87% uptime (approximately 56.7 minutes downtime per month on average)
We missed our SLA target by 0.08 percentage points.

Incidents by Severity

SEV1 (full outage or core feature broken for all users)
3 incidents total, 4.2 hours total downtime

1) July 12: Database failover failure. Duration: 2.1 hours. Users affected: 34,000. Root cause: misconfigured health check caused primary to be marked healthy during network partition, preventing failover. Fix deployed July 15: improved health check logic with partition detection, added manual override capability for on-call.

2) August 28: Payment processing timeout. Duration: 1.5 hours. Users affected: 12,400. Root cause: third-party payment gateway degraded, our 30-second timeout caused thread pool exhaustion cascading to all payment endpoints. Fix deployed September 3: reduced timeout to 5 seconds, added circuit breaker, added fallback queue for delayed processing.

3) September 19: CDN misconfiguration. Duration: 0.6 hours. Users affected: all users briefly. Root cause: deployment pushed wrong origin configuration. Fix deployed September 19: added configuration validation to deploy pipeline, requires sign-off from 2 engineers.

SEV2 (degraded performance or non-core feature broken)
11 incidents total, 18.7 hours total degraded time
Top causes: 4 capacity-related (auto-scaling too slow for traffic spikes), 3 bad deployments, 2 third-party dependency failures, 2 configuration errors
Notable: August 3 auto-scaling failure during marketing campaign. p95 latency went from 200ms to 8.4 seconds for 3.2 hours, 8,900 users affected.

SEV3 (minor issues, workarounds available)
27 incidents total, mostly transient errors, retry-able failures, non-critical background job failures

Incident Response Metrics
- Mean time to detect: 4.2 minutes (target: 5 minutes) ✓
- Mean time to acknowledge: 8.7 minutes (target: 10 minutes) ✓
- Mean time to resolve: 47 minutes (target: 30 minutes) ✗
- On-call page frequency: 2.3 pages per night average (target: less than 1 per night) ✗

Fixes Implemented This Quarter
1. Database health check improvements: $12,000 engineering time
2. Payment timeout reduction and circuit breaker: $8,500 engineering time
3. CDN configuration validation: $4,200 engineering time
4. Auto-scaling threshold and cooldown tuning: $3,000 engineering time
5. Deploy pipeline improvements with canary analysis: $15,000 engineering time
6. On-call rotation expanded from 4 to 6 engineers
Total fix cost: $42,700 engineering time

Remaining Known Issues
1. Auto-scaling still too slow for sudden traffic spikes, needs predictive scaling
2. Database failover runbook is outdated, team not confident in procedure
3. No chaos testing in place, reliability only tested by real incidents
4. On-call burden still high, 2.3 pages per night is unsustainable long-term
5. Payment circuit breaker has not been load tested at production scale

Proposed Actions
1. Implement predictive auto-scaling based on historical traffic patterns. Cost: $25,000 (1 engineer, 4 weeks). Expected impact: reduce SEV2 capacity incidents by estimated 60%.
2. Quarterly database failover drills. Cost: $8,000 per year (4 hours per drill, 4 engineers). Ensures team can execute failover in under 15 minutes.
3. Chaos testing program. Cost: $35,000 setup (2 engineers, 6 weeks) plus $5,000 per quarter ongoing. Proactively finds weaknesses before users do.
4. Hire 2 more engineers for on-call rotation, bringing team to 8. Cost: $380,000 per year total compensation. Brings page frequency below 1 per night.
5. Payment system load test. Cost: $6,000 (1 engineer, 1 week) plus $2,000 infrastructure. Validates circuit breaker under real load.
Total proposed cost: $454,000 ($74,000 one-time plus $380,000 annual)

Risks of Inaction
- Not addressing auto-scaling: likely repeat of August 3 incident during Q4 holiday traffic
- Not hiring: on-call burnout, 2 engineers have expressed intent to leave if on-call situation doesn't improve
- Not doing chaos testing: unknown vulnerabilities remain hidden until they cause incidents

Open Questions
- Who owns the chaos testing program? I don't have a volunteer and the platform team says they're at capacity through Q1 2025. We need someone to own this or it won't happen.
- The hiring question: should we hire 2 new engineers or try to redistribute existing headcount? I don't know if we have budget approval for net-new headcount.

Pricing Experiment Report - Q3 2024

Experiment: August 1 - September 30, 2024 (61 days)
Product: Northwind Professional tier
Current price: $49/month per user
Variants: $39/month (20% decrease), $59/month (20% increase), $49/month (control)
Traffic: 25% each variant, 25% holdout (existing customers)
Total visitors: 84,300 | New signups: 3,247

Conversion Results
- Control ($49): 3.8% conversion, 822 signups
- Low ($39): 4.7% conversion, 1,017 signups (+23.7% vs control)
- High ($59): 3.1% conversion, 671 signups (-18.4% vs control)
Statistical significance: p < 0.01 for both variants vs control

Revenue Projection (60-day)
- Control: $49 × 822 × 0.72 retention = $29,016/month
- Low: $39 × 1,017 × 0.68 retention = $26,970/month (-7.1% vs control)
- High: $59 × 671 × 0.74 retention = $29,330/month (+1.1% vs control)
Low price converts more users but lower per-user revenue and slightly lower retention. High price nearly matches revenue despite fewer conversions.

Caveats
1. Retention data is early (30-60 days), rates could shift significantly
2. Ran during strong sales period, may not generalize to Q1
3. High price variant had higher support ticket rate (12.3% vs 9.1% control), suggesting higher expectations
4. Low price attracted more SMB segment (68% vs 54% control), fewer enterprise leads
5. Did not test price changes for existing customers
6. Sub-segment analysis has wider confidence intervals

Segment Breakdown
1-10 employees: Low price +33%, High price -33% vs control
11-100 employees: Low price +17%, High price -9%
100+ employees: Low price +7%, High price +14%
High price performed better with larger companies, possibly value signaling.

Competitive Context
- Competitor X: $45/month, similar features
- Competitor Y: $65/month, more features
- At $39 we'd be 13% below Competitor X
- At $59 we'd be 9% below Competitor Y

Options
1. Keep $49: lowest risk, stable conversion and revenue
2. Lower to $39: gain SMB market share, accept ~7% revenue hit, brand risk
3. Raise to $59: marginal revenue gain, better enterprise positioning, lower conversion volume
4. Tiered pricing: $39 for SMB, $59 for enterprise (100+ employees). Cost: $28,000, 6-week build, ready late November

Timeline
- Q4 is historically strongest quarter (budget season)
- Price change should be in place by October 15 to capture Q4 demand
- Tiered pricing would not be ready until late November, missing early Q4
- Competitor X rumored to be raising prices Q1 2025

Risks
- Lowering price: hard to raise later, may devalue brand
- Raising price: lose price-sensitive segment that feeds upsell pipeline
- Tiered pricing: sales process complexity, engineering cost
- No change: competitors may undercut us

Open Questions
- Should we invest in tiered pricing even though it won't be ready for early Q4? I don't know if the segment differences justify the $28k cost and added complexity.
- Is the high price variant's higher retention (0.74 vs 0.72) real or just early data noise? We need 2-3 more months to know but Q4 pricing decision is needed now.
